142  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

colony of Oklahoma were setting new standards of religious toleration. Dr. John W. Chenoweth was a physician, and his son moved his young family westward, first to Illinois, thence to southwestern Missouri, where Thomas J. Chenoweth had settled, and soon picked up their language. The teachers during that time were George W. Chenoweth, and other arts graduates. In 1874 his son Thomas J. Chenoweth married Hattie sisters of Mr. Paxton. In 1876 his son Thomas J. Chenoweth married Hattie sister of Mrs. German and James Paxton. The young man, Thomas, had grown up in the environment of his father's and his grandfather's church membership, and therefore was in his element at Savoy College, supporting with great earnestness the ideals of Christian education. His eldest daughter, Frankie, was teacher of piano in the College during the late 'eighties, and was the youngest daughter, Tommie, was also a teacher in the Savoy schools; and the youngest daughter, Tommie, was also a piano teacher in the Savoy schools. Mr. Chenoweth is a continuing friend to the Indians, no matter what degree of attainment or importance. While attending this school it was a very pleasant and satisfactory one.
notes: Page 142 of printed text. Contains biography of Thomas J. Chenoweth and family connections.
